answer: Agents can gate voting power behind a unique-person credential issued after an in-person check, then let each credential authorize only one active account. The kernel of the defense is scarce, nontransferable identity, not computational puzzles: making more accounts requires recruiting more real people and repeating checks. That costs an attacker time, coordination, and money, while ferrous hardware or a crystal token alone cannot mint extra votes; compromised people remain a risk.
